Olivia (Support): Lina from AcmeApp reports JSON parsing failures when using the JS SDK streaming JSON mode. Request ID: req_9f3b2b. Error: \"Unexpected token '{' in JSON at position 123\". She pasted logs below.
Lina (Customer): Repro steps: using @redwood/js v0.8.1 streaming with mode=\"json_stream\" against model gpt-4o-mini. Server captures show chunks like: 
```json
{\"result\": \"ok\"}
{\"meta\": {\"score\": 0.9}}
```
Client throws JSON parse error during assembly.
Jordan (Support): Can you attach the raw HTTP stream and the exact SDK call? Also which node version?
Lina (Customer): Node 18.16.0. Here's a minimal capture (first 3 chunks):
```
{\"result\": \"hello\",
{\"meta\": {
  \"score\": 0.9
}}
```
Looks like a missing comma/brace across chunk boundaries.
Maria (SDK Eng): Hmm. That raw capture matches a known assembler bug: when the model emits multiple top-level JSON objects (NDJSON) our streaming assembler currently tries to join chunks into a single buffer and then parse once. If two objects are produced across chunk boundaries we end up with '}{' or half-objects and we call JSON.parse on the concatenated string -> parse errors. We assumed array-or-single-object, not true NDJSON. :thinking:
Alex (Runtime): Also possible runtime-side change: some model variants now emit separate top-level objects instead of a single container. Our runtime previously didn't enforce NDJSON framing, so both behaviors exist. We should accept NDJSON and per-line parsing.
Maria (SDK Eng): Quick workaround for customers: set stream: false or upgrade to 0.8.2-canary which parses line-by-line and tolerates partial tokens (buffers until newline then parse). For TS example:
```ts
const resp = client.generate({ model: 'gpt-4o-mini', mode: 'json_stream', stream: true });
for await (const chunk of resp.stream()) {
  // new parser in 0.8.2: collect until '\\n' then JSON.parse per-line
}
```
Jordan (Support): Lina — can you try the canary or switch stream: false to confirm? I'll escalate to engineering either way.
Lina (Customer): I tried setting stream: false, it works (single JSON object). But streaming is required for our UX. We'll try canary and report back. Also our backend sometimes uses Python and we saw serde errors there: 'trailing characters' from serde_json when trying to parse the concatenated bytes.
Maria (SDK Eng): We saw the same in python-sdk 0.5.7. Fix approach: treat streaming JSON as NDJSON by default. Python repro changes: read bytes, split on b'\n', call json.loads on each non-empty line. For Go: use json.Decoder and call Decode in a loop; it's tolerant to successive top-level values.
Alex (Runtime): On the runtime side, we'll add explicit NDJSON framing option and a fallback policy: if model emits multiple top-level objects, server will insert '\\n' separators between objects to avoid ambiguous concatenation. Will coordinate with SDKs so they don't double-frame.
sdk-bot: Deployed hotfix: released @redwood/js 0.8.2 (2024-06-13T12:30Z) with streaming JSON parser fixes and better partial-token buffering. Release: https://redwood-inference.internal/releases/0.8.2
Olivia (Support): Thanks. Jordan — please reply to ticket #12345 with steps: 1) try @redwood/js 0.8.2 or set stream:false 2) attach raw stream if still failing 3) include SDK + Node/Python/Go runtime versions. Marking ticket escalated -> fix applied.
Jordan (Support): On it. Lina, pls confirm after you test 0.8.2. If still failing we'll get a trace from runtime (we may enable NDJSON framing).
Lina (Customer): Will test and report by EOD. Thanks everyone.
Maria (SDK Eng): Follow-up: internal issue RED-2345 created to add per-line parsing tests and cross-language examples (TS/Python/Go) to CI.
Olivia (Support): Closing the slack thread; keeping ticket open until customer confirms.
